newsitem.title: USA: Clinton Medicare plan positive -- House budget chair.
newsitem.headline: Clinton Medicare plan positive -- House budget chair.

text.p: House Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich said Tuesday that President Clinton's Medicare savings proposal was positive for the prospects of reaching a budget agreement.
"This frankly brightens, I think, the prospects for being able to get a budget agreement," the Ohio Republican told reporters.

"This gives us good hope ... that we could reach a budget agreement we believe sooner rather than later as a result of the president being willing to come forward and, as he said, move half way," he said.

House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer, R-Texas, said at the same press briefing that he was hopeful Republicans would be able to negotiate an agreement with the White House on capital gains tax relief.

"The White House and the Secretary of the Treasury know that in order to pass a tax bill through the Congress we're going to have to have some sort of broad-based capital gains relief, and I'm very hopeful that we'll be able to negotiate some common ground in that area," he said.
